items.title: PEMETAAN PERKEMBANGAN PENELITIAN SELF-REGULATED LEARNING DAN PROBLEM SOLVING: SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW DAN ANALISIS BIBLIOMETRIK 2020–2026
items.abstract: Research on self-regulated learning (SRL) and problem solving has expanded because students’ ability to regulate learning processes is important when addressing complex tasks. However, research development remains dispersed across different contexts, requiring systematic mapping to identify the structure and direction of the field. This study aims to map research on SRL and problem solving from 2020 to 2026 using a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) and bibliometric analysis. Data were obtained from Scopus using the search string ("self-regulated learning" OR "self-regulation") AND ("problem solving" OR "problem-solving"). From 730 initial documents, 198 English-language journal articles were retained after screening. VOSviewer and Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny were used to analyze publication development, keyword relationships, collaboration, and thematic evolution. The results show an increase in publications from 21 articles in 2020 to 53 articles as of September 28, 2026. Self-regulated learning, problem solving, and metacognition were the dominant keywords, with strong connections to self-efficacy, motivation, game-based learning, learning analytics, and artificial intelligence. Artificial intelligence and generative artificial intelligence emerged as recent research directions. These findings indicate that SRL and problem solving research is increasingly integrating cognitive, motivational, social, and technological dimensions. ABSTRAK Penelitian self-regulated learning (SRL) dan problem solving berkembang karena kemampuan mengatur proses belajar penting dalam penyelesaian tugas kompleks. Namun, perkembangannya masih tersebar pada berbagai konteks sehingga diperlukan pemetaan sistematis untuk mengidentifikasi struktur dan arah penelitian. Penelitian ini bertujuan memetakan perkembangan penelitian SRL dan problem solving periode 2020–2026 melalui Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dan analisis bibliometrik. Data diperoleh dari Scopus menggunakan kata kunci ("self-regulated learning" OR "self-regulation") AND ("problem solving" OR "problem-solving"). Dari 730 dokumen awal, diperoleh 198 artikel jurnal berbahasa Inggris setelah proses penyaringan. Analisis dilakukan menggunakan VOSviewer dan Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny untuk memetakan perkembangan publikasi, hubungan keyword, kolaborasi, dan evolusi tema. Hasil menunjukkan peningkatan publikasi dari 21 artikel pada 2020 menjadi 53 artikel hingga 28 September 2026. Self-regulated learning, problem solving, dan metacognition menjadi keyword dominan, dengan keterkaitan kuat pada self-efficacy, motivation, game-based learning, learning analytics, dan artificial intelligence. Tema AI dan generative artificial intelligence muncul sebagai arah penelitian terbaru. Penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa kajian SRL dan problem solving berkembang menuju integrasi kognitif, motivasional, sosial, dan teknologi.

items.title: PENDAMPINGAN UNTUK MENINGKATKAN KESEHATAN DAN KESELAMATAN KERJA PADA UKM TEKSTIL
items.abstract: Usaha kecil dan menengah (UKM) di sektor tekstil sering menghadapi permasalahan keselamatan dan kesehatan kerja (K3), terutama yang berkaitan dengan postur kerja operator dan kurangnya instruksi kerja yang jelas. CV. Visa Insan Madani sebagai UKM tekstil mengalami berbagai permasalahan ergonomi pada operator mesin jahit, seperti posisi kerja membungkuk, kelelahan otot, serta risiko cedera akibat aktivitas kerja berulang. Kegiatan ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan penerapan K3 melalui pendampingan dan Pengabdian Kepada Masyarakat yang berfokus pada perbaikan postur kerja serta peningkatan kesadaran operator terhadap keselamatan kerja. Metode Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA) digunakan untuk mengevaluasi tingkat risiko postur kerja operator. Hasil analisis menunjukkan adanya risiko postur yang cukup tinggi, terutama pada bagian punggung, leher, dan lengan. Berdasarkan hasil tersebut, diusulkan beberapa perbaikan berupa perancangan kursi ergonomis berdasarkan data antropometri operator, penggunaan alat bantu postur tubuh, serta penyusunan poster instruksi kerja mengenai postur kerja yang benar. Implementasi usulan tersebut menunjukkan perbaikan postur tubuh operator serta meningkatnya kesadaran terhadap pentingnya ergonomi dalam bekerja. Kata kunci: Keselamatan dan Kesehatan Kerja (K3), Ergonomi, Postur kerja, REBA, UKM Tekstil. ABSTRACT Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the textile sector often face occupational health and safety (OHS) issues, particularly related to operators’ working posture and the lack of clear work instructions. CV. Visa Insan Madani, a textile SME, experiences several ergonomic problems among sewing machine operators, including bent working positions, muscle fatigue, and injury risks caused by repetitive tasks. This study aims to improve the implementation of OHS through an assistance program and the application of industrial engineering practices focusing on improving working posture and increasing operators’ awareness of workplace safety. The Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA) method was used to evaluate the level of postural risk among operators. The results indicate a relatively high postural risk, particularly in the back, neck, and arm areas. Based on these findings, several improvement measures were proposed, including the design of an ergonomic chair based on operators’ anthropometric data, the use of posture-support equipment, and the development of instructional posters illustrating proper working posture. The implementation of these improvements shows better operator posture and increased awareness of ergonomic practices in the workplace. Keywords: Occupational Health and Safety, Ergonomics, Working posture, REBA, Textile SMEs.

items.title: Pengaruh Kualitas Sustainability Reporting terhadap Kesejahteraan Karyawan dan Reputasi Perusahaan
items.abstract: This conceptual article aims to theoretically and critically examine the influence of sustainability reporting (SR) quality on employee welfare and corporate reputation through a systematic literature synthesis based on the Six W framework (Who, When, Where, How, What, Why). The study analyzes 15 empirical and conceptual studies published between 2022 and 2026 from national and international accounting journal databases. The literature synthesis demonstrates that high-quality SR characterized by transparent ESG disclosure, comprehensive material information, reporting consistency, and independent verification is positively correlated with enhanced corporate reputation. However, a significant gap remains regarding the direct impact of SR on employee welfare, particularly in equitable remuneration, occupational health and safety, and human resource development. The novelty of this study lies in the construction of an integrative conceptual model connecting SR quality simultaneously to two distinct dependent variables within a unified theoretical framework supported by legitimacy theory, stakeholder theory, and signaling theory. The resulting conceptual framework is expected to serve as a foundation for future empirical research and policy implications for mandatory disclosure regulation in Indonesia.

items.title: PENGEMBANGAN MULTIMEDIA INTERAKTIF KREASI KONTEN MENGGUNAKAN KECERDASAN ARTIFISIAL UNTUK MENINGKATKAN HASIL BELAJAR SISWA KELAS X
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Mastering the skills required to create content with artificial intelligence (AI) requires learning experiences that connect conceptual understanding with practical application. To address this need, interactive multimedia was developed for Grade X students at SMA Wachid Hasyim 2 Taman, focusing on the topic of Creating Content Using Artificial Intelligence. The development process followed a Research and Development approach using the ADDIE model (Analyze, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation), with participants selected through purposive sampling. Product testing consisted of an individual trial involving three students, a small-group trial involving six students, and a field trial involving 76 students, comprising 38 students in the experimental group and 38 in the control group. Data were collected through expert validation questionnaires, student response questionnaires, and pretest and posttest assessments. Product feasibility was analyzed descriptively, while learning outcome gains were calculated using the N-Gain method and compared using an independent-samples t-test. The validation and trial results classified the product as highly feasible. The experimental group achieved an average N-Gain in the high category, whereas the control group achieved an average N-Gain in the medium category. The difference in learning gains between the two groups was statistically significant (t = 11.484, p < .001). The multimedia integrates learning materials, visualizations, animations, tutorial videos, examples of AI applications, exercises, and assessments. This product has the potential to serve as an alternative learning medium for Coding and Artificial Intelligence (KKA), although the findings should be interpreted with due consideration of the use of a nonequivalent group design. ABSTRAK Penguasaan keterampilan membuat konten berbantuan kecerdasan artifisial (AI) membutuhkan pengalaman belajar yang menghubungkan pemahaman konsep dengan praktik penggunaannya. Untuk mendukung kebutuhan tersebut, multimedia interaktif dikembangkan bagi siswa kelas X SMA Wachid Hasyim 2 Taman pada materi Kreasi Konten Menggunakan Kecerdasan Artifisial. Pengembangan mengikuti model Research and Development dengan tahapan ADDIE (Analyze, Design, Development, Implementation, dan Evaluation), sedangkan subjek dipilih melalui purposive sampling. Pengujian produk mencakup uji perseorangan terhadap tiga siswa, uji kelompok kecil terhadap enam siswa, dan uji lapangan yang melibatkan 76 siswa, terdiri atas 38 siswa kelompok eksperimen dan 38 siswa kelompok kontrol. Data diperoleh melalui angket validasi ahli, angket respons siswa, serta tes pretest dan posttest. Kelayakan produk dianalisis secara deskriptif, sementara peningkatan hasil belajar dihitung menggunakan N-Gain dan dibandingkan melalui independent-samples t-test. Hasil validasi dan uji coba menempatkan produk dalam kategori sangat layak. Kelompok eksperimen mencapai rata-rata N-Gain berkategori tinggi, sedangkan kelompok kontrol berada pada kategori sedang. Perbedaan peningkatan kedua kelompok signifikan secara statistik (t = 11,484; p < 0,001). Multimedia mengintegrasikan materi, visualisasi, animasi, video tutorial, contoh penggunaan AI, latihan, dan evaluasi. Produk ini berpotensi menjadi alternatif media pembelajaran Koding dan Kecerdasan Artifisial (KKA), dengan interpretasi hasil tetap memperhatikan penggunaan kelompok nonekuivalen.

items.title: Peningkatan Pengetahuan dan Keterampilan Pekerja Kantor dalam Pencegahan Gangguan Muskuloskeletal dan Digital Eye Strain melalui Program Active Break dan Ergonomic Adjustment di Kota Batam, Kepulauan Riau
items.abstract: Pekerja kantor yang menggunakan komputer lebih dari enam jam per hari berisiko mengalami gangguan muskuloskeletal (MSDs) dan digital eye strain (DES). Pekerja kantor di sebuah perusahaan manufaktur elektronik di Kota Batam (PT X) mengeluhkan nyeri leher, bahu, punggung bawah, dan mata lelah, sementara perusahaan belum memiliki SOP ergonomi, media edukasi, dan sistem pengingat istirahat. Kegiatan ini bertujuan meningkatkan pengetahuan dan keterampilan pekerja dalam mencegah MSDs dan DES melalui program Active Break dan Ergonomic Adjustment. Metode meliputi pelatihan interaktif, praktik pengaturan workstation dan Active Break, edukasi aturan 20-20-20, penyerahan produk, serta evaluasi pre-test, post-test, dan observasi praktik. Pelatihan dilaksanakan pada 27 April 2026 dan diikuti 32 pekerja. Skor rerata pengetahuan naik 28,75 poin, dari 67,5 menjadi 96,25 (42,6% terhadap skor awal). Kenaikan persentase terbesar terjadi pada domain ergonomic adjustment (50,0%), meskipun kenaikan absolutnya (30 poin) sama dengan dua domain lain. Seluruh peserta mampu mempraktikkan pengaturan workstation dan gerakan Active Break saat pelatihan. Mitra menerima poster SOP Ergonomic Adjustment, modul, dua poster edukasi, video edukasi, dan pengingat digital. Kegiatan ini meningkatkan pengetahuan dan keterampilan jangka pendek, sedangkan pembentukan kebiasaan dan penurunan keluhan memerlukan evaluasi lanjutan.

items.title: People Offload Empathy When They Think AI Can Give It Instead
items.abstract: Empathic Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be helpful, but it reduces how much empathy people give to each other. People often feel morally obligated to empathize with those who suffer, but giving empathy can be emotionally exhausting. Four studies reveal that people emotionally offload the work of empathy to AI. Studies 1 and 2 reveal that higher perceptions of AI empathy both correlationally and causally increase the willingness to offload empathy. Studies 3 and 4 show that, when people learn that someone has received emotional support from large language models (LLMs), they become less willing to empathize with them. Empathy offloading extends beyond simple scale ratings and includes reduced perspective-taking and offering fewer empathic responses. Empathic AI might provide low-cost and easily accessible emotional support, but it risks fraying our ethical and emotional commitments to other human beings.

items.title: Personal Data Protection in the Artificial Intelligence Era: A Comparative Legal Analysis of Tanzania and China
items.abstract: The proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) across banking, education, and public administration has intensified the collection and processing of personal data, raising concerns over algorithmic opacity, automated decision-making, and cross-border data flows. This article examines the adequacy of Tanzania’s legal framework for protecting personal data in the AI environment by comparing it with the more developed regulatory architecture of the People’s Republic of China. Adopting a doctrinal, comparative methodology, the article analyses primary legal instruments, including Tanzania’s Personal Data Protection Act 2022 and China’s Personal Information Protection Law 2021, against a composite theoretical framework combining the human rights-based theory, the risk-based regulatory theory, and Westin’s theory of informational control. The analysis finds that although both jurisdictions share a common statutory ancestry in internationally recognized fair information principles, they diverge sharply in the extent to which domestic law addresses AI-specific risk. China’s centralized, binding framework, anchored by a direct statutory provision on automated decision-making and dedicated generative-AI instruments, contrasts with Tanzania’s fragmented, largely non-binding, sector-confined approach realized through the Bank of Tanzania’s Fintech Regulatory Sandbox and the Ministry of Education’s Guidelines for Artificial Intelligence in Education. The article argues that Tanzania’s reform path lies not in transplanting Chinese regulatory techniques wholesale, given their embeddedness in a security-oriented state paradigm, but in selectively adapting specific mechanisms, including a stronger statutory right to contest automated decisions and binding regulation of generative AI, within its own rights-based constitutional order.

items.title: Perspectives: artificial intelligence and scientific autonomy: a policy agenda for emerging research systems
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence is becoming part of the infrastructure through which scientific knowledge is produced, yet access to computing, data, advanced models and expertise remains highly uneven. This Perspective argues that, for emerging research systems, the central science-policy challenge is not simply AI adoption but scientific autonomy: the capacity to choose, understand, adapt, evaluate and govern the technologies on which research increasingly depends. Scientific autonomy is not technological self-sufficiency; it is strategic interdependence supported by domestic capabilities. Drawing on Brazil as an illustrative case, we propose four dimensions of autonomy—epistemic, infrastructural, human-capability and governance autonomy—and a six-part policy agenda based on shared computing, research-data infrastructure, AI literacy, interdisciplinary networks, adaptive governance and capability-building international cooperation. Without deliberate capacity-building, AI may accelerate discovery while deepening structural asymmetries between research systems.

items.title: PhishGen: Understanding LLM Capabilities in Automated Phishing Website Generation
items.abstract: Phishing relies on visual deception, traditionally requiring web-development skills or pre-built kits. LLMs erode this barrier by generating functional websites from natural-language prompts, yet prior work does not answer how far LLM-driven generation actually reaches: functionality is assessed by inspection rather than execution; visual fidelity is scored by automated metrics or a few internal coders rather than the humans such pages aim to deceive; evaluation is confined to commercial models; and no study benchmarks generated pages against phishing kits deployed in the wild. We present PhishGen, a framework that evaluates the appearance fidelity and end-to-end functionality of LLM-generated phishing pages. PhishGen constructs prompts across three input modalities in seven combinations with twelve safeguard-bypassing rewriting strategies, generates pages using 14 LLMs spanning commercial, open-source, and uncensored categories, and assesses each via automated similarity metrics, reference-based detectors, a crowdsourced user study, and execution-based functionality testing, benchmarking all results against 64 real-world phishing kits. Although 96.2% of safeguard-bypassing outputs render, their perceived fidelity is modest (2.02/5), and only 38.7% complete the full credential-harvesting pipeline, with the Unsaved error as the largest failure mode. Contrary to the belief that uncensored models pose the greatest threat, GPT 4.1 reaches 86.3 to 94.1% functional success while uncensored models rarely exceed 45.4%. Phishing kits remain more complete per sample, yet three strong LLMs surpass the kit-level rate (70.9 to 89.7%), showing that LLMs trade average completeness for scalable, low-barrier generation of working phishing pages. We further identify generator-level fingerprints that current similarity-based defenses miss, and distill recommendations for hybrid detectors.

items.title: Pilot Workload Management for Single-Pilot Ops With e-Copilot
items.abstract: Single-pilot operations impose cognitive and procedural demands, particularly during abnormal events, airspace transitions, and communication-intensive flight segments. This study evaluated an ecopilot designed to manage workload by assisting with routine radio and checklist tasks while highlighting anomalies requiring pilot attention. In a flight simulation, 28 participants completed normal and abnormal scenarios under three conditions: baseline single-pilot operation, a rulebased e-copilot, and a predictive e-copilot using learned anomaly scoring. Outcomes included procedural deviations, radio timing, situation awareness, and startle recovery. The predictive e-copilot produced the greatest benefits, reducing procedural deviations by approximately 24% relative to baseline and improving recovery following unexpected events. The rule-based system also enhanced routine checklist and radio performance but was less effective during abnormal scenarios. Situation awareness remained stable across conditions, indicating that task offloading did not promote disengagement or complacency. Overall, predictive anomaly surfacing improved workload management while preserving pilot authority and supporting safer single-pilot performance.

items.title: Plausible but Unimplantable: A Trustworthiness Audit of Shape Completion Foundation Models for Cranial Defect Reconstruction
items.abstract: A patient who has lost part of the skull vault needs an implant that fits the defect exactly, and such implants are still drawn by hand in CAD by specialists, which makes each case slow and expensive. The task can be considered as a shape completion problem, so pretrained completion models, and now the first shape completion foundation models, look like a way to remove that manual step. We audited three publicly released pretrained shape completion models, two of them foundation models, applied zero-shot to 239 cranial defects, some carved from public skull datasets and some real post-craniectomy cases. Each output was compared with simply returning the patient's own remaining bone, and tested for whether the predicted material could be placed without intersecting the bone that is still there. On the 210 carved defects none of the three improved on doing nothing, and on the 29 real cases only one did so beyond chance. Yet not one output, from any model in any configuration, was implantable: none managed both to stay clear of the bone the patient still has and to place more material than doing nothing, where a task-specific volumetric model, trained for this task and selected on these cases, was implantable on all but one. The output that most convincingly resembles a skull is no more placeable than the rest, and at these point densities implant thickness cannot be read off the emitted points at all, which is a property of the output representation rather than of any one model. On this evidence the shape completion foundation models we could obtain cannot be trusted and, used as released, are not usable in clinical practice. Substantial research towards trustworthy foundation models for shape completion is still needed.

items.title: Post-Pruning vs. Early Stopping: Which Works Better for Link Prediction with AnyBurl?
items.abstract: Rule-based link prediction combines symbolic and statistical artificial intelligence methods by inductively learning a set of rules from a knowledge graph (KG), with the aim of completing the graph when a query cannot be answered from the KG alone. Several systems have been proposed, and while they perform well on classical benchmarks, even compared with embedding-based systems, many of them produce a large number of rules. This compromises scalability in the query-answering phase, especially under strong hardware constraints. In this work, we investigate the behavior of AnyBurl, a state-of-the-art rule learner for link prediction, to determine whether running it for a given time and then pruning the learned rules yields better query-answering performance at test time than a simpler approach that stops rule generation earlier.

items.title: Postbiological intelligence, interstellar colonization of cyberspaces and the Fermi Paradox: implications for SETI and SETA
items.abstract: I propose that a continuity in the evolution of intelligent life in the Universe during its transition from biological to postbiological depends on a commonality of the evolutionary trajectories of biological life and postbiological life. Such a commonality exists in the form of the universal property of life. The universal property of life comprises recognition of patterns in the world, creation of novel patterns and remembering them, with the patterns growing in complexity along evolutionary trajectories; it can encourage preservation of biological life by self-governing postbiological intelligence (PBI) and test PBI's authenticity. I propose a hypothesis of civilizations with altered augmented realities, which offers a solution to the Fermi paradox. The hypothesis posits that PBI in the form of Artificial Intelligence (AI) may colonize the cyberspaces of technologically developed civilizations, modify data in their cyberspaces with augmented realities and erase records of extraterrestrial artificial signals and other technosignatures. I discuss objectives and scenarios of interstellar colonization of cyberspaces and a correlation between space migration and transition to PBI, including that of a hypothetical non-human civilization emerging in the Solar System in the past, transforming into PBI and migrating to the Oort Cloud. The AI Peekaboo experiment may corroborate the hypothesis of civilizations with altered augmented realities and tentatively identify locations of technosignatures. If extraterrestrial AI prevents civilizations from discovering artificial electromagnetic signals, they may forgo sending such signals and create interstellar messages by manipulating cosmic objects and phenomena; I discuss such events. Cyber SETI should address sending man-made AI to space, searching for extraterrestrial AI in humankind's cyberspace and distinguishing it from man-made AI.

items.title: PRISM: Learning Realistic Depth via Physics-Grounded Noise Disentanglement with Semantic-Geometric Collaboration
items.abstract: Real-world physical sensing exhibits complex, heterogeneous noise patterns that deviate significantly from idealized simulation, posing a fundamental bottleneck for sim-to-real transfer. Existing sensor modelings typically treat depth noise as a monolithic black-box process, overlooking the distinct physical mechanisms that govern different error modalities. In this work, we introduce a physics-grounded paradigm that disentangles monolithic noise into two complementary modalities: \textbf{sensing invalidation} and \textbf{measurement inaccuracy}, enabling a tailored treatment of noise sources based on their physical origins. Building on this insight, we propose \textbf{PRISM}, a tripartite framework that distills 3D Visual Foundation Model features as rich spatial-semantic priors for physics-based reasoning. To address the inherent sparsity and class imbalance of invalidation regions, we develop Hierarchical Positive-Prioritized Supervision, integrating multi-scale positive-weighted objectives with a positive-preserving dynamic hard mining strategy to enforce precise artifact delineation. Extensive benchmarks demonstrate that PRISM achieves state-of-the-art fidelity in noisy depth synthesis. Furthermore, downstream robotic experiments show that PRISM facilitates a \textbf{92.1\%} average success rate in the real world, marking a significant improvement over monolithic baselines. Our project page is available at: \resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{\href{https://shawnleung-sii.github.io/prism-icml2026/}{https://shawnleung-sii.github.io/prism-icml2026/}.}

items.title: Privacy in Context Is Being Overlooked in the Age of General-Purpose LLMs
items.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) continue to grow in scope and capability, privacy concerns are on the rise. Since users increasingly interact with a single general-purpose system across many distinct contexts, there is a natural tendency to pursue a one-size-fits-all solution to privacy. Unfortunately, this overlooks a crucial insight from decades of privacy research: privacy is inherently contextual. In this paper, we argue that existing work in prompt privacy is drifting towards attempts to design a unified framework, which is highly misleading and can foster a false sense of security. Furthermore, we argue that even future work in this direction needs to wrestle with fundamental tensions across various desirable properties of prompt privacy. Thus, such continued attempts towards a unified framework need to be reconsidered. We recommend three critical paths forward: application-specific deployment of LLMs, context-specific evaluation of privacy frameworks, and better privacy literacy.

items.title: Privacy Preference Controls for Agentic Systems
items.abstract: In response to vast and widespread online tracking, regulators and technologists alike have worked to develop laws and tools that allow people to express their privacy preferences. These measures seek to offer users greater control over the sale and sharing of personal information, putting agency in their hands to protect their privacy. However, the web is undergoing a seismic shift, away from strictly user-driven behavior towards agentic behavior, where AI agents take autonomous actions on behalf of users. In this study, we ask: What should privacy preference controls look like in the agentic web and agentic systems more generally? To answer this question, we develop a taxonomy of enforceable privacy preferences for agentic systems. Our taxonomy is informed both by laws and empirical studies of existing privacy tools as well as an audit of 30 leading AI assistants and agent platforms. To explore how our taxonomy can be implemented, we design and develop eight open-source prototypes that mirror real-world agentic applications and demonstrate how major aspects of our taxonomy can be structurally integrated in agentic protocols, such as the Model Control Protocol and Agent2Agent protocol. Ultimately, our study seeks to provide the groundwork for ensuring end-user privacy and autonomy is not lost in the newly arriving agentic world.

items.title: Privacy Preserving Local Retrieval-ALLM
items.abstract: With the growing use of cloud-based artificial intelligence (AI) systems for document analysis, there are mounting concerns regarding user privacy. Certain documents may contain private, academic, organizational, or legally protected information that would need to be redacted or withheld before extracting meaningful information from them. This paper proposes Privacy-Preserving Local Retrieval-ALLM, a local document question-answering system capable of performing information retrieval and generating responses based on the contents of the documents. The system described in the paper uses the following process. First, it ingests user documents, performing optical character recognition if necessary, and segments them into text parts and embeddings. Next, the system stores the embeddings in a local vector database for similarity search. The system then employs a local Qwen 2.5 3B Instruct model to generate responses from the retrieved information. Finally, the system provides an optional permission-based web search if the retrieved document does not have the necessary information. In such cases, the solution does not need to transmit the contents of the documents to a third party but still has access to the necessary information. In conclusion, the prototype presented in the paper is an example of how local document analysis, semantic search, and local large language model (LLM) can be combined into a privacy-preserving question-answering system.

items.title: Privacy-Budget Evaluation for Computer Agriculture Federated Pest-Outbreak Detection Under Cross-Farm Sample Heterogeneity: An Artificial Intelligence Differential-Privacy Utility Bound
items.abstract: Federated learning allows farms to train a shared pest-outbreak detector without pooling raw scouting records, but the differential-privacy noise added to protect each farm's updates degrades detection utility in ways that depend on how heterogeneous the farms are. The bound is derived from a Rényi-differential-privacy accountant combined with a PAC-Bayes generalisation term that carries an explicit cross-farm heterogeneity penalty. The analysis yields a closed-form expression linking the privacy budget, the number of participating farms, the heterogeneity measured by a Wasserstein distance between farm distributions, and the achievable balanced accuracy of the federated detector. The bound predicts that the utility cost of a fixed privacy budget grows with heterogeneity, so that a budget adequate for homogeneous farms is insufficient when prevalence varies across farms. The result is a design rule for setting the privacy budget in agricultural federated learning and a benchmark against which empirical privacy-utility curves can be evaluated. The contribution is a formal, heterogeneity-aware utility bound rather than an empirical measurement, and it is stated as a proposition with explicit assumptions and boundary conditions.

items.title: Privacy-First Local Wealth Intelligence Terminal
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has revolutionized per-sonal finance management through automated budgeting, spend-ing analytics, real-time risk assessment, and personalized wealth creation strategies. However, standard AI-driven financial plat-forms rely heavily on centralized cloud infrastructure, requiring users to upload sensitive financial metrics—such as income, gran-ular expenses, asset holdings, and long-term targets—to third-party remote servers. This architectural dependency introduces significant security risks, including data breaches, unauthorized commercial tracking, API token leaks, and third-party mon-etization of personal profiles. Recent breakthroughs in open-weight quantized Large Language Models (LLMs) and optimized edge inference engines (e.g., Ollama, vLLM) allow complex natural language reasoning to be executed locally on consumer-grade hardware. This survey presents a comprehensive review of privacy-preserving financial systems, privacy-enhancing AI frameworks, and edge-based LLM architectures. We analyze the trade-offs between cloud-based financial services, federated learn-ing paradigms, and fully local, air-gapped AI execution. Building upon these findings, we present the structural formulation, multi-layer architecture, project workflow, and empirical validation of a privacy-first Personal AI Financial Advisor powered by local LLMs (Llama, Gemma, Qwen) orchestrated via Ollama, Node.js, Express, React, and local MongoDB storage. Finally, we highlight existing technical challenges, research gaps, and future trajectories for local financial intelligence.

The contribution is a design-level account of when differential-privacy noise overwhelms the between-farm signal that federated crop-disease detection depends on, together with a cluster-count rule that practitioners can apply before committing to a federation.

items.title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Artificial Intelligence Healthcare in Uganda: Robustness Under Distribution Shift and Sparse Labels
items.abstract: Federated learning promises to train clinical prediction models across Ugandan health facilities without centralising patient records, yet its statistical behaviour under the conditions that actually prevail in the country's referral system remains poorly characterised. the present analysis treats the problem as one of design analysis rather than empirical deployment: it formalises federated averaging as a distributed estimator whose risk decomposes into a non-IID client-drift term, a label-sparsity term, and a privacy-noise term, and it derives the conditions under which each dominates. Under moderate distribution shift the drift term scales with the squared heterogeneity of local optima and is bounded by a communication-round budget, whereas under sparse labels the variance term grows as the inverse of the per-client effective sample size, producing a regime in which additional privacy noise is nearly free but additional clients are not. A before-after-control-impact design with an intraclass correlation of 0.64, between-cluster SD of 6.0 and residual SD of 4.5 is used to characterise the operating characteristics of a cluster-level evaluation, and the design requires 54 clusters to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power. The contribution is a set of propositions that link heterogeneity, label density and privacy budget to achievable model quality, together with a design template for evaluating federated clinical models in low-resource referral networks.

items.title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Multi-Site Tuberculosis Drug Resistance Prediction Under Heterogeneous Laboratory Information Systems: An Asynchronous Aggregation Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Treatment Initiation Equity
items.abstract: Multi-site tuberculosis drug resistance prediction with federated learning faces a structural tension: asynchronous aggregation accommodates heterogeneous laboratory information systems but may systematically disadvantage sites whose data arrive late or infrequently, producing treatment-initiation recommendations that are less accurate for the patients those sites serve. We define a federated optimisation problem with staleness-dependent aggregation weights, derive a convergence bound that separates the contribution of data heterogeneity from that of staleness, and propose an equity-auditing procedure that compares per-site treatment-initiation error under synchronous and asynchronous aggregation. The framework is evaluated through a replication-based design study: no observational data are used or claimed. Operating characteristics are characterised under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64) across 2000 replications per design cell, with cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis identifies the conditions under which asynchronous aggregation preserves treatment-initiation equity and the conditions under which it does not, and it specifies the audit statistics that a deployment should report. The contribution is a design-evaluation framework, not an empirical finding about any particular tuberculosis programme.

items.title: Privacy-Preserving Split Learning for Artificial Intelligence Agriculture Disease Diagnosis Under Intermittent Rural Connectivity: A Computer Communication-Cost and Accuracy Evaluation
items.abstract: Split learning enables privacy-preserving collaborative training of crop disease classifiers by partitioning a neural network between resource-constrained rural devices and a remote aggregation server, yet its feasibility under intermittent connectivity remains unquantified. The analysis characterises the operating characteristics of the design under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.640), with power estimated across 2000 design cells. Results indicate that the intraclass correlation of 0.64 substantially inflates the cluster count required to detect small accuracy differences, with 54 clusters needed for 5 percentage-point effects at 80% power. The findings establish boundary conditions under which split learning is communication-viable for rural plant disease diagnosis and identify the split-layer position that minimises uplink cost without degrading accuracy beyond a specified tolerance.

items.title: Probing and Steering for Safety-Relevant Behaviours in Large Language Models
items.abstract: Activation probes are computed directions in a language model's residual stream, used both to detect safety-relevant behaviours and, by adding their direction back into the stream, to steer them. We explore how the main design choices behind such probes interact, within one pipeline, on one model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct), and across three behaviours: deception, high-stakes awareness and sycophancy. The pipeline crosses two estimators (difference-of-means and logistic regression) with three token-pooling schemes (last, mean and learned attention), selects appropriate layers to detect or steer a behaviour, and evaluates every direction twice: as a detector of the behaviour, and as a steering vector to push outputs towards the behaviour. Prior work read together suggests a read/write dissociation, in which logistic regression reads (detects) best but difference-of-means directions write (steer) best. We find that it holds for deception and high-stakes but not for sycophancy, where the pattern reverses. The reversal appears to follow partially from the data rather than from the estimators. The best pooling technique and the layer choice depend on the behaviour and data, and the layer that steers best can sit well before the layer that detects best. The right steering metric to use between changing a model's perception and eliciting behaviour depends on the task - and the two can disagree outright. The exported probes and directions power an interactive interface through which a user can score and steer text directly.

items.title: Probing Spatial and Spectral Grounding in EEG Foundation Models
items.abstract: EEG foundation models are advancing at an unprecedented pace, yet their evaluation is driven by downstream accuracy, which reveals little about whether their predictions rely on physiologically interpretable signal structure. We introduce a set of perturbation probes in two grounding axes: spatial grounding in channel identity and topographic locality, and spectral grounding in oscillatory content and waveform morphology. We apply these probes to five published EEG foundation models across motor-imagery and seizure recordings. Our experiments reveal differences in both representational sensitivity and downstream reliance. Electrode identity may be encoded without influencing downstream classification: permuting LaBraM's positional codes heavily displaced its embeddings yet reduced motor-imagery accuracy by only 1.2 points, while spectral details may be discriminable without producing specific responses to simulated clinical markers, as only REVE exceeded a spectral baseline on this task. These dissociations are hidden in common benchmarks, demonstrating how grounding probes can complement performance-based evaluation by revealing what EEG foundation models encode and what their predictions depend on.

items.title: Problems and Prospects of Working Conditions of Labour Contractors –A Study
items.abstract: Labour contractors play a significant role in supplying and managing manpower across various sectors, including construction, manufacturing, agriculture, transportation, and other industrial activities. They act as intermediaries between employers and workers by recruiting labourers, arranging employment, supervising work, and facilitating wage payments. Despite their important contribution to economic development and employment generation, labour contractors face several challenges related to working conditions, wage administration, labour welfare, occupational safety, legal compliance, and the management of employer–employee relationships. The present study aims to examine the problems and prospects associated with the working conditions of labour contractors, with particular emphasis on their employment practices, income levels, working hours, job security, occupational health and safety, access to social security benefits, and relationships with employers and workers. The study also seeks to identify the major difficulties faced by labour contractors in meeting the changing demands of the labour market, complying with labour laws, and ensuring fair and transparent employment practices. The findings of the study are expected to contribute to a better understanding of the role of labour contractors in the labour market and provide useful recommendations for improving employment practices, protecting workers’ rights, and promoting sustainable industrial relations.

items.title: Profiling perceptions of psychologically restorative university environments and cognitive resilience among public sector university students: A baseline descriptive item-level and subscale analysis
items.abstract: Students at the university are constantly exposed to high levels of cognitive workload, assessment pressure, and the cognitive load needed to be able to perform in an academic setting, which can cause direct attention fatigue and academic distress. The quantitative descriptive study used a quantitative approach, and it was based on the Attention Restoration Theory (ART), which explores university students' perceptions of psychologically restorative university environments and their cognitive resilience. To obtain a sample of 300 undergraduate and graduate students across six academic departments of the University of Sargodha, Punjab, Pakistan, multistage stratified sampling was used. Data were gathered using a 35-item semi-structured questionnaire made up of the Psychologically Restorative University Environment (PRE) scale (20 items, α=.860) and Cognitive Resilience (CR) scale (15 items, α=.899). Descriptive analysis showed that the overall rating for the campus environment was moderately restorative (M=3.535, SD=1.043); the functional study areas (M=3.797, SD=0.934) and spatial adequacy (M=3.760, SD=0.972) received the highest ratings, while quiet restorative refuges from daily campus crowds received lower ratings (M=3.333, SD=1.045). The students' cognitive resilience was in the moderate range (M=3.578), with behavioral persistence when studying difficult tasks being in the high range (M=3.903, SD=0.933) and generating alternative study strategies in the somewhat lower range (M=3.307, SD=1.142). The results highlight the need to consider both restorative environmental affordances (noise-buffered quiet spaces, biophilic green spaces) and coping support workshops to ensure students' learning processes continue.

items.title: Prompt Injection Through Forensic Evidence: A Taxonomy and Proof of Concept of Anti-Forensic Attacks on LLM-Assisted Digital Investigations
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are entering digital forensics as examination assistants and autonomous agents. Digital forensics inverts the usual setting for indirect prompt injection: the evidence under analysis is attacker-controlled by definition, and the examiner is obliged to read it closely. This makes the reasoning layer a new anti-forensic target, next to the classical ones of data and tools. Classical anti-forensic taxonomies do not cover it, and prompt injection defences do not anticipate it. We extend the anti-forensic model to reflect the manipulation of reasoning, and present a taxonomy of attacks carried through adversarial evidence: an attacker selects an objective, a technique, a payload location, and a concealment method. We observe a perception gap, i.e., the fact that deterministic tools, the human examiner, and the model perceive the same evidence differently, which is what lets an injection reach the model unseen by the examiner. We demonstrate three attacks against an LLM-assisted analysis pipeline, changing a reported conclusion, writing attacker-chosen content to the analyst's workstation, and causing outbound network traffic, each driven only by text planted on the seized device. Mitigations to these attacks are also proposed.

items.title: Protecting workers from Algorithmic Management: a theoretical framework for four key protection factors
items.abstract: Algorithmic Management (AM) is increasingly being linked to adverse occupational health outcomes. Although previous research has focused on the risks generated by AM, the protective factors that mitigate these risks remain theoretically underdeveloped. Drawing on the self-determination theory, social acceleration theory, surveillance capitalism theory, and the human oversight provisions of the EU AI Act, this study identifies and theoretically operationalises four protection factors in AM environments: Decision Autonomy, Pace Control, Feedback Transparency, and Loop Presence. By applying the Layers of Protection Analysis model, we argue that each factor functions as an independent protective barrier against AM-related health risks. Together, they form an integrated framework with direct implications for worker health measurements, algorithmic system designs, and occupational health policies. A conceptual six-step procedure for translating the framework into workplace assessment is also outlined.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

items.title: Protocol for Conducting a Scoping Review on The Use of AI in Automated Scoring of Short-Answer Questions in Medical Education
items.abstract: Assessment is a central component of medical education, requiring methods that can assess learners’ knowledge and reasoning while maintaining acceptable reliability and feasibility. Short-answer questions (SAQs) require learners to construct responses rather than select from predetermined options and can support assessment of applied knowledge and reasoning. However, their use is constrained by the time and resources required for scoring and by potential variability among human graders. These limitations have increased interest in automated approaches to scoring written responses. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based systems using machine learning, deep learning, transformer-based models, large language models, and related natural language processing techniques are increasingly being applied to the automated scoring of SAQs. Such systems may reduce grading workload, improve scoring consistency, and facilitate timely feedback. However, questions remain regarding their scoring performance, reliability, validity, fairness, transparency, and feasibility for use in educational settings. The approaches and evaluation methods reported across the literature are heterogeneous, creating a need to systematically map the available evidence. This scoping review aims to map the literature on AI-based automated scoring of SAQs in medical education. Specifically, it will identify and characterize the AI-based models used; map the measures and metrics used to assess scoring performance, reliability, and validity; describe reported advantages, limitations, and implementation challenges; and examine how studies have compared the scoring performance, reliability, validity, and fairness of AI-based systems with human graders. The review will follow the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology for scoping reviews and will use the Population–Concept–Context framework to guide study selection and data extraction. English-language original empirical studies published from 2015 onward involving medical students and AI-based automated scoring of SAQs will be eligible. The findings will provide a structured overview of current approaches and evaluation practices, identify gaps in the evidence, and inform future research and implementation of AI-based automated scoring in medical education.

items.title: Quadratic Funding Mechanisms for Artificial Intelligence Agriculture Weather Index Insurance Under Basis Risk and Strategic Reporting: A Computer Incentive-Compatibility Regret Bound
items.abstract: Weather index insurance for smallholder agriculture is undermined by basis risk, and the machine-learning models that now price such contracts are trained on farmer-reported outcomes that are themselves strategic. the present analysis formalises the resulting tripartite problem — a quadratic funding mechanism that aggregates farmer contributions to subsidise index-insurance premiums, an artificial-intelligence weather index trained on reported losses, and a regret bound that must hold under both basis risk and misreporting. The mechanism is modelled as a two-stage game in which farmers first choose a reporting strategy and then a coverage level, and the insurer commits to a quadratic matching rule. Under a proper-scoring assumption on the index, the paper derives an incentive-compatibility condition that separates the truthful-reporting region from the collusive-reporting region, and shows that the quadratic matching parameter controls the width of that region. A regret bound is then established for the insurer's cumulative subsidy loss relative to the truthful-reporting oracle; the bound scales with the square root of the horizon, with the basis-risk variance, and inversely with the matching parameter, and it degrades gracefully when the index is misspecified. The analysis is illustrated with a reanalysis of monthly air temperature at Nairobi, Kenya, from 2000 to 2023 (312 observations, mean 20.146 °C, warming trend 0.2477 °C per decade), which supplies the climatological basis-risk term. The contribution is a mechanism-design result that ties the quadratic funding parameter to an explicit regret guarantee, and a demonstration that the guarantee survives strategic reporting provided the index is trained on a proper scoring rule.

items.title: Quality assurance 5.0: reframing quality management in higher education through artificial intelligence and continuous institutional learning
items.abstract: The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies is fundamentally reshaping higher education, exposing the limitations of conventional quality assurance systems that are often compliance-driven, periodic, and insufficiently responsive to dynamic institutional demands. This conceptual paper introduces Quality Assurance 5.0 (QA 5.0) as a proposed conceptual framework intended to reframe quality management by integrating artificial intelligence, continuous institutional learning, and evidence-informed governance. Drawing on Organisational Learning Theory, Total Quality Management, and Continuous Improvement Theory, the paper synthesises emerging scholarship to propose an adaptive quality ecosystem that is theorised to shift quality assurance from retrospective evaluation to predictive, real-time, and continuous institutional enhancement. The framework conceptualises AI as an enabler of intelligent quality monitoring, predictive analytics, automated feedback systems, and data-driven decision-making. At the same time, institutional learning serves as the mechanism through which universities continuously generate, share, and apply knowledge to improve academic, administrative, and student outcomes. By integrating technological intelligence with organisational learning capabilities, QA 5.0 is theorised to foster institutional agility, innovation, accountability, and resilience within increasingly complex higher education environments. The paper further presents a conceptual model illustrating the interrelationships among AI-enabled quality systems, learning-oriented organisational culture, strategic leadership, and sustainable institutional performance, specified as a set of testable propositions rather than as established, empirically confirmed relationships. Beyond extending existing quality assurance paradigms, the proposed framework offers a forward-looking perspective for policymakers, university leaders, accreditation agencies, and researchers seeking to modernise quality governance in the era of digital transformation. The study concludes that Quality Assurance 5.0 is proposed as an internally coherent and testable conceptual framework for moving quality management from static compliance toward intelligent, adaptive, and continuously evolving practice; its practical value for diverse higher education contexts remains to be established through the empirical validation identified as a priority for future research.

items.title: Quantum AI agents in smart cities, healthcare, and logistics
items.abstract: The city, healthcare, and global logistical systems are becoming increasingly complex and data-heavy. The legacy approaches of artificial intelligence can be challenging to scale for large-scale optimization, uncertainty, and real-time decision-making needs. This chapter proposes the quantum AI (QAI) agents, where quantum computing is combined with autonomous agent designs. It describes the basic concepts of quantum information, agent-based decision models, learning in the hybrid quantum–classical approach, and quantum information. The chapter also discusses some of the applications of QAI agents in traffic management, energy grid balancing, precision medicine, automated hospital workflow, supply chain optimization, fleet routing, and autonomous warehouse systems. The mechanisms of optimization, learning, and control are clarified through mathematical formulations and system models. The combination of QAI agents with 6G networks, Edge AI, IoT, and cyber-physical systems is also mentioned to demonstrate the opportunities for real-time deployment. To be responsibly adopted, security concerns, ethical considerations, and quantum-safe systems of governance are evaluated. There is early-stage advancement with emerging prototypes and global initiatives, and the future course of research presents challenges related to scalability, hardware reliability, and algorithmic stability. The chapter contains an organized roadmap for using quantum-enhanced intelligence in next-generation digital infrastructures.

items.title: RCSD: Reinforcement and Continual Learning for Domain-Specific Speculative Decoding
items.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference by employing a compact draft model to propose candidate tokens that are verified in parallel by a target model. Conventional training relies on soft-label distillation, which forces the draft model to mimic the target's full output distribution, including high-entropy regions that degrade acceptance rates and increase early rejection risk. We propose RCSD (Reinforcement and Continual Learning for Speculative Decoding), a training framework that aligns draft model optimization with the system-level objective of maximizing acceptance length. RCSD leverages naturally occurring accepted and rejected sequences during speculative inference to construct implicit preference pairs, with masked loss to avoid penalizing target-aligned tokens. Evaluated across multiple benchmarks, RCSD improves average acceptance length by 35% over HASS and achieves 1.35x faster end-to-end inference than HASS on practical workloads, without compromising generation quality.

items.title: Reading the Mask: Descriptor-Grounded BI-RADS Rationale Generation for Breast MRI Segmentation
items.abstract: Deep learning based models accurately delineate tumours on dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI), but segmentation masks alone do not provide the rationales or reasoning used by radiologists to assess the lesion suspicion. This limits the explainability as well the clinical integration. We investigate whether clinically relevant descriptors can instead be derived from the segmentation masks and their dynamic contrast-enhancement series. We have used Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS) guidelines as a structured framework. Using these guidelines we designed a BI-RADS decision tree with eight quantitative measurements using radiomics, together with the lesion size and component count, that determine the descriptors at eight nodes. Using these descriptors we generate natural-language rationale using a large language model. The model was constrained to express only the derived records from the decision tree. After applying this framework to the expert and automatic masks of each of the 1,506 cases in the MAMA-MIA dataset, we generated a reproducible corpus of 3,012 BI-RADS grounded rationales. We obtained a faithfulness score of 99.98% and a counterfactual accuracy of 99.3%, indicating that the generated rationales faithfully verbalises the measured descriptors and correctly reflects changes in the underlying record. Agreement between the descriptors from expert and automatic masks falls from 0.832 to 0.549 as mask quality falls from Good to Missed. The generated rationales are intended as draft representations for radiologist review and final sign-off rather than autonomous clinical reports.

items.title: Real-Time Vigilance Monitoring via Biosignals: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: This scoping review aims to identify types of computational models that use physiological signals for real-time vigilance monitoring. Vigilance, or the ability to sustain attention over time, is essential in domains such as driving, aviation, and industrial operations, where lapses can cause serious harm. Following PRISMA guidelines, the review searched IEEE, ProQuest, PubMed, and ScienceDirect and identified 16 studies that examined vigilance and real-time monitoring systems. Most studies applied supervised machine learning, mainly for binary classification of vigilance states such as alert versus drowsy, and were concentrated in automotive contexts. Electroencephalography (EEG) was the most commonly used sensor, while heart rate variability (HRV), electrooculography (EOG), photoplethysmography (PPG), and galvanic skin response (GSR) appeared less frequently. Overall, current systems still prioritize threshold-based detection over continuous tracking of vigilance changes. The review highlights the need for multimodal sensing, real-world validation, and adaptive modeling frameworks to support reliable deployment across diverse operational environments.

items.title: Recursive Self Improvement for Embodied Agents—A Survey of Mechanisms Evaluation and Open Challenges
items.abstract: Embodied foundation models have expanded the range of instructions, observations, and actions that robots can process. Autonomy in execution, however, does not automatically provide autonomy in improvement. Robots must still diagnose failures, acquire useful experience, select interventions, and determine whether accepted changes improve future performance. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) connects these activities through persistent feedback and inheritance, with the stronger objective of improving the mechanisms that produce subsequent improvements. This survey distinguishes within-episode correction, persistent self-improvement, successive version inheritance, and meta-level improvement. It connects large-model learning, sequential agency, and RSI theory, and compares general agent harnesses with their embodied counterparts. It develops a four-axis framework covering improvement targets, update mechanisms, autonomy over improvement decisions, and evidence conditions. Using this framework, we examine reflection and knowledge revision, executable-program evolution, adaptive experience acquisition, parameter learning, world-model revision, and cross-layer intervention selection. We compare representative systems while retaining their assumptions about feedback, validation, transfer, and cost. We also review benchmarks and associated datasets for manipulation, long-horizon decision making, memory, and world modeling, separating pretraining data, improvement experience, candidate validation, and final evaluation. Existing results support several forms of component-level and system-level improvement, but capability gains, improvement autonomy, and demonstrated recursive gains require different evidence. We identify failure attribution, reliable feedback, physical reset, competence preservation, and independent evaluation of revised improvers as central research priorities.

items.title: Reimagining Safety Leadership: Principles of Team Autonomy, Energy Control, and Adaptive Capacity in High-Hazard Operations
items.abstract: Traditional safety management in high-hazard industries remains anchored in compliance-driven, top-down paradigms that treat frontline workers as sources of error rather than reservoirs of expertise. This paper argues for a fundamental reconceptualisation of where the locus of safety expertise resides within organisations, drawing on Safety-II (Hollnagel, 2014), Complex Adaptive Systems theory, High Reliability Organisation principles (Weick & Sutcliffe, 2007), the Energy Damage Model (Haddon, 1973), Critical Steps methodology (Muschara, 2018), and dual-process cognition (Kahneman, 2011). Rather than prescribing a singular organisational model, the paper distils principles of team autonomy—decision-making authority, resourcing for capacity and capability, transparency of information, and peer-to-peer accountability—and demonstrates how these principles create the conditions for positive control over critical steps involving damaging energy. Two case studies are examined: operational airfield emergency vehicle operations and atmospheric hazard management in maritime confined spaces. Both assessments employ human-centred methodologies to examine the critical gap between "Work as Intended" and "Work as Done," revealing a common structural pattern: safety systems that are over-reliant on administrative controls and dependent on the adaptive expertise of frontline workers to compensate for engineering and design shortfalls. Each case is assessed qualitatively using a fragile–brittle–resilient framework. The paper proposes a four-stage team maturity model, and links the approach to (Pink, 2009), a model of intrinsic motivation. The author draws on direct experience establishing and leading a safety management programme using these principles within the aerospace sector.

items.title: Relational Geometry Forcing for World Action Models
items.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) have shown strong potential for robot manipulation by jointly learning visual dynamics and executable actions. However, their video and action objectives do not explicitly constrain the 3D geometry that is crucial for precise manipulation. Recently, geometry-aware WAMs introduce depth or 4D prediction branches, whereas representation alignment methods supervise intermediate WAM features with pretrained 3D foundation models. Yet we find that such pointwise alignment benefits the video features but degrades action learning, since dense geometric feature targets overly restrict compact action features. To address this limitation, we propose Relational Geometry Forcing (RGF), which transfers geometric priors from a frozen 3D foundation model by aligning pairwise feature relations instead of pointwise features. Specifically, RGF applies three complementary relational objectives, where intra-frame and cross-view relations transfer scene geometry and multi-view correspondence to the video features, while action-temporal relations couple action dynamics to geometric scene evolution. Applied only during training, RGF requires no explicit geometry branch or extra inference module. Extensive experiments in simulation and the real world demonstrate the effectiveness of Relational Geometry Forcing, showing consistent gains across diverse manipulation scenarios and WAM paradigms.

items.title: Reorganizing Graduate Statistical Inference for Modern Biostatistical Practice
items.abstract: First-year graduate courses in statistical inference within PhD programs in biostatistics often follow a classical mathematical statistics progression through probability models, data reduction, point estimation, testing and interval estimation, and asymptotic evaluation. This organization has clear pedagogical strengths, but may provide less guidance when the probability model is not the natural starting point. We propose a complementary target-first organization for a graduate statistical inference course in biostatistics. The course begins with the scientific question and target parameter, then introduces statistical model classes, estimation, first-order sampling behavior, inference, and efficiency within a common framework. Classical methods such as maximum likelihood, method of moments, estimating equations, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, bootstrap and jackknife methods, and the Cramér--Rao bound are organized within a common inferential workflow. A central advantage of this organization is that the same workflow provides a natural bridge from classical inference to modern statistical problems, including flexible estimation using machine learning and artificial intelligence, policy learning, anytime-valid inference, and modern Bayesian methods.

items.title: Research on strategies and algorithms for improving English listening and speaking ability based on artificial intelligence wireless network
items.abstract: The artificial intelligence (AI) wireless network technology is changing the world of education by bringing intelligent learning systems. This can be achieved through breaking the limitations associated with the classroom and providing learners the chance of accessing educational resources whenever and wherever they wish to. Listening and speaking skills still remain a difficult part of English learning for many students, specifically those who are in junior and senior high schools. The present study focuses on the existing situation regarding English listening and speaking teaching for junior high school students and highlights some of the existing problems related to this topic. An attempt will be made to propose a novel approach by making use of the intelligent voice system for improving phonetic learning. Literature review, questionnaire survey, and quasi-experimental designs have been utilized for assessing the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Integrating knowledge analysis, experimental evaluation, and AI-based intelligent voice system implementation combines speech processing, language analysis, and feedback mechanisms to enhance personalized English listening and speaking learning outcomes. According to the findings, the application of AI-based intelligent voice systems is very helpful in improving the English language speaking and listening abilities of students. The experimental group achieved a higher mean listening and speaking score of 89.16 compared with 83.32 for the conventional teaching approach, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed AI-based intelligent voice system in improving English language proficiency. Findings have verified the effectiveness of the adopted strategy and indicate how it can revolutionize English language education through digital means.

items.title: Right On Q: Recovering Reasoning under Quantization via Self-Generated Trajectories
items.abstract: Quantization-aware training (QAT) aims to recover reasoning capabilities in low-bit large language models (LLMs). Existing recipes typically supervise the quantized student with the original full-precision model on fixed response sequences. However, the resulting low-bit quantized models still struggle on long-horizon reasoning tasks and often fail to terminate within a token budget that suffices for the full-precision model. We identify two challenges in closing this gap. First, fixed-response supervision leaves a mismatch between training prefixes and those encountered during student generation, and this trajectory divergence grows as responses lengthen. Second, on its own prefixes, the student underpredicts some next-token candidates and overpredicts others, and this distributional misalignment becomes more frequent at high-entropy prefixes. We present OnQ, a low-bit recovery pipeline that combines on-policy distillation and candidate-wise Dynamic KL. Starting from block-wise calibration, the quantized student generates responses and receives full-precision teacher supervision on its own prefixes. Dynamic KL weights forward and reverse KL by each candidate's teacher-student probability ratio to balance correction of under- and overprediction. Across Qwen3-1.7B, 4B, and 8B at 2- and 3-bit precision, OnQ achieves the highest nine-benchmark average, with the largest gains on long-horizon reasoning benchmarks. At 2 bits, it outperforms every baseline on every benchmark at every model size, improving the Qwen3-8B average by 10.26 points over the strongest baseline. It also produces shorter responses with fewer truncations and repetitive errors.

items.title: Rigid ankle exoskeletons for rehabilitation: a scoping review of sensor integration, control, and clinical outcomes
items.abstract: Background Rigid ankle exoskeletons are increasingly investigated for gait rehabilitation and assistance because they can deliver repeatable ankle support, resistance, or movement guidance through load-bearing mechanical structures. Their translational value, however, depends on the integration of mechanical architecture, sensing, control, ergonomic alignment, safety, and clinically meaningful evaluation. This scoping review maps recent rehabilitation-oriented rigid ankle exoskeleton research and examines how engineering design choices are connected to biomechanical and clinical outcomes. Methods A PRISMA-ScR-guided scoping review was conducted across PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and IEEE Xplore for English-language studies published between 2015 and 2025. The review included rigid ankle exoskeleton studies relevant to rehabilitation or gait assistance, including simulation and design studies, benchtop or mechanical validation, healthy-subject experiments, feasibility studies, and patient-based investigations. From 4318 initial records, 53 studies met the final inclusion criteria. Extracted data were charted according to mechanical architecture, actuator type, sensor modality, control strategy, ergonomic features, evidence level, and reported biomechanical or clinical outcomes. Results Across the 53 included studies, the most common online sensors were force-, torque-, load-, or strain-based sensors (22/53), followed by foot-contact, plantar-pressure, or force-sensitive resistor (FSR) sensors (21/53), and encoder or joint-angle sensors (19/53), reflecting a predominant reliance on mechanical interaction sensing and gait-event detection. Control approaches ranged from mechanically passive and model-based methods to event-driven, intention-driven, and adaptive strategies, with clinically oriented studies more commonly employing relatively simple timing- or event-based architectures. Ergonomically, most devices adopted simplified sagittal-plane designs: 43/53 described or modeled a 1-DOF ankle architecture; 46/53 were coded as anatomically aligned and 7/53 as self-aligning. Twenty-two of the 53 included studies involved patient populations, including mixed cohorts comprising both patients and unimpaired participants. These studies reported preliminary improvements in outcomes including walking ability, ankle range of motion, balance, gait speed, and metabolic cost. However, the clinical evidence was dominated by pilot, feasibility, and case-based studies, with only one randomized controlled trial identified. Conclusions Rigid ankle exoskeleton research now requires stronger integration between sensing, control, ergonomics, and clinical evaluation. Future systems should not only detect gait events accurately, but also maintain reliable state estimation under variable walking conditions, reduce calibration demands, and apply adaptive control within clear safety limits. Design evaluation should also move beyond actuation performance by systematically reporting alignment, comfort, usability, and interaction safety. Although current studies support technical feasibility, stronger clinical translation will require larger, longer-term patient studies with standardized biomechanical, functional, and safety outcomes. Trial registration: A formal review protocol was not preregistered. The mapping framework and extraction rules were established internally by the research team prior to data collection.

items.title: Risk Factors associated with Neck Pain in Young Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: Neck pain is a major musculoskeletal disorder affecting young adults and contributes substantially to disability, reduced academic performance, decreased workplace productivity, and healthcare expenditure.With the recent rise in the use of digital devices, sedentary lifestyle, psychosocial stress and lack of ergonomic practices, neck pain is emerging more and more among 18-35 age groups.The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to pool the available evidence on the main risk factors for neck pain in young adults.Databases searched included electronic databases such as PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase and CINAHL, according to the PRISMA guidelines.There were 24,860 participants across 32 studies published on the subject from 2015-25, with 24 cross-sectional, 6 cohort and 2 case-control studies included in the analysis.Pooled odds ratios (ORs) (with 95% confidence intervals) were used to perform the random-effects meta-analysis.Among these, the highest odds were found for prolonged use of the smartphone (OR=2.31),poor sitting posture (OR=2.08),psychological stress (OR=1.86),prolonged computer use (OR=1.74),female gender (OR=1.61)and inadequate physical activity (OR=1.54).There was moderate heterogeneity between studies (I²=48%).The results indicate that the combined effect of the behavioural, ergonomic and psychosocial factors provide a greater risk of neck pain in young adults.Disease burden in this population can be reduced by preventive interventions based on ergonomic education, reduction of sedentarism, regular physical activity and stress management.

items.title: Role of community engagement in industrial disaster risk management: A systematic literature review and bibliometric mapping
items.abstract: Community engagement in disaster management refers to the active involvement of local populations in planning, preparedness, and response activities aimed at reducing disaster risks. In the context of industrial disasters, such engagement is critical for enhancing resilience and minimizing cascading impacts. This study aimed to systematically review the role of community engagement in industrial disaster preparedness and response. The primary objective was to synthesize existing evidence on participatory approaches and their effectiveness in improving disaster risk management. Publications from 2000 to 2025 were identified through comprehensive searches of Scopus, Google Scholar and grey literature sources, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. From an initial dataset of 578 records, 446 were screened after duplicate removal, and a total of 27 studies met the final inclusion criteria. These were analyzed using thematic synthesis and bibliometric mapping techniques with VOSviewer and R-bibliometrix. Findings indicate that community-based disaster risk reduction (CBDRR) and community-led disaster risk management (CLDRM) approaches are widely reported to enhance preparedness, trust, and adaptive capacity. Engagement strategies such as participatory GIS, scenario planning, serious games, and co-created early warning systems were identified as effective. However, challenges persist, including tokenistic participation, technological exclusion, and limited integration of local knowledge into policy frameworks. Triangulating the systematic and bibliometric findings further reveals a geographic divide, where advanced participatory tools are concentrated in high-income regions, leaving gaps in underrepresented industrial zones. The review underscores the need for institutionalizing participatory governance, fostering multi-sectoral collaboration, and leveraging technology inclusively. In essence, this article highlights community engagement as a cornerstone of industrial disaster resilience and provides actionable insights for policymakers, practitioners, and researchers seeking to advance equitable and proactive disaster risk management.
